question: Who among the following is considered the first Tirthankara of Jainism?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rishabhanatha**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• Tirthankara of Jainism
 
 
• In Jainism, a Tirthankara is a saviour and divine guide on the dharma (righteous path).
 
• The word "Tirthankara" refers to the creator of a "**samsara," **or fordable route through the sea of limitless births and deaths.
 
• According to Jains, a Tirthankara is a person who, by himself, has conquered "samsara," the cycle of rebirth and death, and created a way for others to follow.
 
• The Tirthankara attains "Kevala Jnana" after realising his or her actual nature as spirit or self.
 
• Rishabhanatha is the first Tirthankara ("ford-maker") of Jainism and the creator of the Ikshvaku dynasty born to king Nabhi Raja and Queen Marudevi at Ayodhya
 
• Abhadeva, Rishabhadeva, and Abha are other names for Rishabhanatha.
 
• According to Jain tales, he lived millions of years ago.
